caption:
An American general paddled ashore in a canoe at night, hid in a wine cellar from the police, and went home without his trousers. It was one of the most important secret meetings of the war.

22 October 1942. Major General Mark Clark landed from the British submarine HMS Seraph near Cherchell, Algeria. At a seaside villa he met French General Charles Mast and U.S. diplomat Robert Murphy. Clark needed the French army in North Africa to help the coming Allied landings, not fight them.

Mast agreed. Then the local police, tipped off by the servants, came knocking. The Americans dropped into the cellar while their hosts faked a drunken party upstairs.

Escaping in heavy surf, Clark stripped off his trousers so the gold coins in his money belt would not drag him under. A canoe was lost, and the gold with it. Clark made it back to Seraph. Seventeen days later came Operation Torch.
